Thor - Mercury Mayhem [5710]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Mercury has been poisoning workers and the environment for over 30 years. Even though there has been a comission of enquiry and interventions by the Government the mercury stock pile still exists.

In September last year it was reported that ;
Thor Chemicals to pay R300m to remove its deadly mercury waste from KZN
The department of environmental affairs says it wants more than 3,000 tons of mercury waste stockpiles at the old Thor Chemicals factory in KwaZulu-Natal to be removed by the end of next year.
The department says Thor Chemicals — a British multinational that owned and ran the Cato Ridge plant where drums of toxic sludge are stored — has agreed in principle to pay more than R300m required to export the waste to Switzerland, where it will be disposed of.
Mercury is a powerful neurotoxin, which can lead to blurred vision, tremors, brain damage, coma and death. In the late 1980s and 1990s, scores of Thor Chemicals workers who were exposed to the hazardous chemical waste were diagnosed with mercury poisoning and died painful deaths. Others were partially poisoned and are still feeling the effect of this poisoning, decades later.
Thor Chemicals moved its mercury incinerator plant from Margate, Kent, in the UK in the mid-70s after an outcry about the hazardous nature of the operation. The company then began exporting these chemicals to its Cato Ridge facility. The plant was forced to shut its doors here in the early 1990s after news that workers poisoned by mercury were dying and others were comatose. The plant has been in a state of dilapidation since then.
Two incidents have shone the spotlight on the plant in recent months. Criminals stole some containers of the toxic substance in the hope of using it in zama-zama mining pursuits and other criminal activities. A few weeks ago, a fire broke out at the facility, and environmental organisations estimate that more than 30 tons of mercury waste was injected into the environment as a result of the fire.
In August 2019, the minister of environmental affairs, forestry and fisheries, Barbara Creecy, promised to take immediate action to ensure that the chemicals were moved from the site and destroyed. Albi Modise, spokesperson for the department, said talks between government officials and Thor Chemicals are at an advanced stage.
“Our laws stipulate that the perpetrator must pay for the cleanup. Minister has made it clear that this mercury-containing waste must be disposed of appropriately and expeditiously. The option proposed by Thor Chemicals entails the removal of the waste to a company that is based in Switzerland. This company has a sound track record of dealing with mercury and mercury-containing waste and has the necessary capacity and authorisations to do so. The department’s primary concern is the safe and expeditious disposal of the waste to avoid any environmental harm,” Modise said.
Neville Naicker, a director of Thor Chemicals SA subsidery, Guernica has in the past declined to speak to journalists.
Bobby Peek, director of environmental lobby group groundWork, said pressure from local environmental organisations on the one hand and local communities on the other had forced the government to finally take action after more than two decades of neglect.
“We have always maintained that the waste stockpiles can only be treated outside SA because we have never had the facilities to deal with mercury toxic waste locally. This mercurial waste should never have come to SA in the first place. The toxic waste sludge is made up of a mixture of mercury sludge, arsenic and other organic compounds, making it difficult to treat,” Peek said. He added that the government must also consider the plight of scores of former Thor Chemicals workers.
“There are many [former] workers and families who were affected by the Thor Chemicals operation and we believe they have never received a just and fair long-term settlement commensurate with the loss they suffered,” he said.

Talbot Tests
Pse check my maths

From our test results the cow tail was 0,97 mg/kg - can one assume that the meat would be the same amount? In other words the cow tail is 20 times higher than the allowed limit?

The highest water we tested was a sediment sample at 772, if one compares that to natural mineral water it is 772 000 times higher. But can one assume that the sediment is the same as the water?

Are there any prescribed values of how much mercury is allowed in the soil?

People to Interview
We already have a confront with us and Thor.
Tinto Summerton – worked at Thor for 13 years. Was paid out R160 000 for compensation but says his health is still affected. Interviewed
Enoch Nkosi – Worked at Thor for a year. Was dismissed when he started showing symptoms of mercury poisoning. The workers were never told they were handling was toxic. They were not given any protective gear.
Ground Work – Either Bobby Peak or Rico Euripido. Highly versed in subject.
Angela Mathee - Director of the SA Medical Research Council’s Environment and Health Research Unit.
Guernica Interview – Neville Naicker?
Minister Barbara Creecy – Forestry and Fisheries and Environmental Affairs has visited Thor when the warehouse burnt down last year. They have had two mysterious fires.
Bill Lambrecht – journalist broke the story in 1989.
Dennis Davis – Mandela Comission of Enquiry . Stated Governments culpability in the toxic waste imports and found both the apartheid government and Thor complicit. Gov was to set up a system to tear waste and Thor would have to pay to have it treated.
Green Scorpions?
Umgeni Water?

Thor Holdings was a manufacturer of mercury comtaining products based in Margate UK since the 1970s. In the 1980s after health concerns were raised and the company was therarened with prosecutio, it closed down its operatioons and moved its plant to Cato Ridge KZN, where it opened in 1988 as one of the world’s largest reclamation facilities. At the time, countries around the word were abandoning incineration as a means of processing harzardouse waste but regulations in South Africa were lax.
The question is why did a British company such as Thor decide on South Africa to build the largest recycling plant in the world? The obvious answers which spring to mind are: - South Africa's poor environmental protection laws;
- cheap and repressed labour;
- no established popular environmental non-governmental organisations;
- a hope that political outcry over apartheid might leave little time for environmental activities.
Within a year, water samples in the nearby Mngweni River showed 1500 times the level considered toxic. By 1992 at least one worker has died from mercury poisoning and there were reports that 28% of the workforce had suffered exposure. Two workers have died.
According to the workers that I have interviewed they were not warned of the toxicity of the working envioronment. They also were not proivided with any protective gear. An additional problem was that some of the waste was stolen by people who wanted the drums and possibly by illegal miners.
The alarm was raised in the Natal area when three independent investigations, one by the Umgeni Water Board, another by a US newspaper, the St.Louis Post-Dispatch and a third, by the environmental group Greenpeace International, revealed alarmingly high deposits of mercury at the source of the Mngeweni River, just below Thor Chemicals. In an analysis of soil and sediment samples performed by the Queen Mary College in London, a sediment sample was found to be contaminated by 1 764 parts per million of mercury - this is 8 810 times the US standard for classifying the waste as hazardous. River sediment samples at Fredville were also well above the US standard for hazardous wastes.
When members of Earthlife Africa spoke to workers at the plant they were told that two workers had "gone mad". They were taken to hospital as they were "doing and saying strange things, and were shaking a lot". These are typical symptoms of mercury poisoning. The Managing Director at Thor said that workers did get sick but they did not
"go mad". "We check the guys* urine every week and if levels exceed 200 micrograms of mercury per litre they are given orange juice to drink and taken away from the plant."

Mercury Madness Final Script

V/O
This is the pastoral Valley of a Thousand Hills, the tranquility of this scene belies a dangerous reality. Livestock from the area drink from this small stream that has been contaminated with the poisonous heavy metal - mercury.

V/O
And the mercury has come from here, Thor Chemicals a couple of hundred meters up stream.

Link REDO BEGINNING OF LINK
“These warehouses behind me ARE where hundreds of tons of mercury waste from all over the world have been stored for over 30 years.”

V/O
Thor Chemicals was a company that made a range of mercury based products and used to be based in Margate, England.

Link
In the late 70s, Thor left the UK after it had transgressed environmental laws so they packed up , lock stock and barrel and brought what the UK Gov had flagged as health and safety hazards here to South Africa.

V/O
They opened a plant to recycle mercury waste.
And it wasn’t just a barrel or two, it is estimated that over 3000 tons of toxic waste was shipped here from all over the world. To give perspective of the volume imagine 3000 one ton bakkies.

http://www.bluebulbprojects.com/measureofthings/results.php?comp=weight&unit=tns&amt=3000&sort=pr&p=1

V/O
In the 70’s and 80’s, South Africa’s environmental laws for were quite lax says Musa Chamane.

Musa
“We did not have any legislation that prevented any waste entering the country or so on, so they took advantage of that policy vaccuum.”




V/O
Chamane is an environmentalist at GroundWork in Pietermaritzburg. They are one of the organisations that is pressurising the government to take action to prevent more environmental contamination.

Link
This is the Mngceweni River which flows down from Thor chemicals and makes its way to the Umngeni river, which feeds into the Inanda Dam. Now the last water samples that we made available were done ages ago, so we took some samples of our own.

V/O
These are two toxic sludge dams on the Thor property and over time mercury from here has leached into the environment, either through the dams overflowing during floods or by accident.


V/O
Eight samples of soil, sediment and water were sent to Talbot Laboratories in Pietermaritzburg.

V/O
The fence result was 16.2 (milligrams of mercury per kilogram of soil) showing that there was contamintion across Thor’s fence. The sediment samples in the over flow dam were very high at 330 and 772.

Mercury concentrations which exceed 50 mg per kilogram in sediment is classified as chemical waste.
V/O
Prof Jacques Oosthuizen is an epidemiologist at Edith Cowan University in Perth. He wrote his doctorate on the Thor Chemical’s mercury poisoning and
says it is an exceptionally dangerous neurotoxin.


https://www.environment.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/situation_analysisof_mercury_sa.pdf

(Page 41)

Jacques
“It affects the nervous system, its blurred vision reduced IQ, problems concentrating, appears person is drunk. Its horrible, its neural and it gets worse over time.”

V/O
Enock Nkosi who is helping Chamane take water samples, used to work as a chemical process operator at Thor Chemicals and knows first hand how it affects one.

Enock
‘Sometimes in the morning I stumble around like I’m drunk but I don’t drink and I don’t smoke. I find myself feeling weak like I am drunk.

V/O
In 1993 a comission of enquiry was initiated by President Nelson Mandela to probe why the previous government allowed Thor to import the toxic waste. He visited Thor Worker Engelbert Ngcobo in hospital, before he died from mercury poisoning. Judge Dennis Davis, who chaired the Commission found both the apartheid government and Thor complicit.

https://www.groundwork.org.za/archives/2019/news20190826-Deadly_Mercury_Injected_into_the_Air.php


Enock
“I don’t speak as fast as I used to, and now I have a stutter”

V/O
Many of the tests in the past have focussed on the Thor workers, but can mercury be detected in the community living downstream? The residents do have tap water but some still drink from the river and see as a valuable resource.




Chris
“The ladies when they have got these cultural things, they often come down here in the morning and go to the river to go and wash themselves.”

Sindi
“It’s a problem if there is poison in the river because sometimes the kids go and swim in the river and they will be affected.”

V/O
Sipho Meyiwa is a cow herd for 3 families who have collectively lost 10 cows at the beginning of the year.


Sipho
‘When I saw them coming from the river they looked weak and some of them died by the river and we just left them there.”

V/O
The cow deaths may be anecdotal, but no tests were conducted to see whether the mercury played a part or not.

V/O
Richard Spoor is a human rights lawyer who has successfully held the mining industry accountable in his billion rand settlement on behalf of the workers who were affected by silicosis.


Richard Spoor
“Animals dying after drinking contaminated water is a strong indicator that something is wrong in the environment. We have seena lot of this in the Highveld where the cattle have been dying from drinking contaminated water from a waste disposal dams on the coal mines.”


V/O
To find out if there was any mercury in the hair of residents, cows or goats, samples were taken and sent to the lab.

Masa
“You have had a look at the samples, what were the results?”

Jacques
the Carte Blanche samples were detected and their level was 2.6 which is signigicantly higher than the permissable level.”


Jacques
“It does appear that it is getting through the ecosystem through livestock and I don’t know what levels will be in milk or meat of those animals.”

V/O
This is Minamata Bay in Japan, where the world’s most horrific mercury poisoning disaster took place. From 1932 – 1968 Chisso Corporation, a fertiliser company, dumped 27 tons of mercury laden waste in the bay. To date over 1700 people have died as the mecury contaminated the whole food chain
The mercury caused severe damage to the brain and nervous system, leading to a condition now called Minamata disease.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minamata_disease

Tinto
“This one guy living next door to me, he got sick and when we came here at work, this guy when he drinks a cup of coffee he will go past his mouth with a cup of coffee he will go this way, and I thought. Whats happening with him, I actually thought he was drunk.”


V/O
Tinto Summerton worked at Thor Chemicals for about 12 years and he says his health is still severely compromised.

Tinto
“I only found out when guys were sick that we are dealing with another thing here and there were already 2 guys in hospital and that is when I realised that ay this thing is most dangerous.”

V/O
In the 80’s Oosthuizen worked at Natal Medical School.

Jacques
“We became aware of patients that had been admitted into our occupation healthward and they had renal failure, which was attributed to mercury exposure, we then worked out that they all worked at Thor Chemicals.”

Tinto
“They never told me how dangerous this stuff was, they never even issued me with a mask.”

V/O
Richard Spoor was employed by NUMSA in the early 90s to represent the Thor Workers against the Department of Labour .

Richard
“There were a number of deaths and people who were very severly disabled and unequivocally poisoned by mercury, there were also blood tests that demonstrated excessively high levels of mercury in their blood.”

Jacques
“When the workers got affected the government shut down Thor and told them they can’t operate any more but of course there were ship loads of mercury waste on their way still there and so the stock pile was just growing and growing and drums were rusting and they were leaking and it just became an absolute disaster waiting to happen.”

V/O
Prof Rajen Naidoo is the Head of UKZN’s Occupational Health Task Team and in the 90’s they monitored the health of the workers.

https://disa.ukzn.ac.za/sites/default/files/pdf_files/ChJul92.1024.8196.000.039.Jul1992.17.pdf

Masa
“Has Thor Chemicals compensated any of the workers?”

Rajen
“It was fined and the fine that was levied on the company was R 13 500 and subsequently the company was taken to court in the UK courts , they eventually settled out of court and the settlement from which the workers that were affected benefitted.”

V/O
Thor Chemicals de amalgamated and the local branch was renamed Guernica in 2000 and Metallica, a sister company took over the Cato Ridge Facility. In the UK settlement, Thor paid 240 000 pounds for the 20 workers who claimed they were victims of mercury poisoning.

https://allafrica.com/stories/201909030225.html
https://www.newframe.com/thor-chemicals-toxic-waste-goes-up-in-flames/


Tinto
“We only got money that just helped us to be able to go to the doctors and I wouldn’t even call it a compensation but it helped us, we are still alive.”


V/O
We requested an interview with Thor Chemicals and sent them a list of questions. They answered by saying,
“The legacy mercury stockpile is under the authority of the Department of Environment, Forestry and Fisheries.”
And we should direct our queries to them.

V/O
They did however call the police when they saw the film crew outside their fence.

Up Sound
“I have been watching you. If we have a break in I am going to hold you responsible.”


V/O
Both Governments have failed to hold Thor accountable. There are no local facilities capable of recycling this waste, there have been proposals of entombing the waste in concrete forever or shipping it back to the senders or to a company in Switzerland for recycling at a cost of about R330 million.

https://allafrica.com/stories/201909030225.html

https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/sunday-times-1107/20190901/281784220766799


Richard
“The government needs to take action against the South African subsideries and compel them to clean up and they simply havent done that.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Creecy

Link
Minister of Environmental Affairs, Forestry and Fisheries, Barbara Creecy went on a fact finding mission in August last year and she said, and I quote, “This is a scandal and a gross irresponsibility on the part of Thor Chemicals.”

https://www.enca.com/news/thor-chemicals-must-clean-mess-creecy

V/O
Less than 2 weeks after the Minister’s visit, a fire broke out in a warehouse storing the mercury waste. It is estimated that as much as 30 tons of mercury was injected into the environment as a result of the fire.

https://www.ban.org/news/2019/8/26/deadly-mercury-injected-into-the-air-a-very-convenient-fire-governments-failure-means-thor-chemicals-will-never-be-held-accountable


Link
“A year later it seems nothing has happened.
We asked the Minister for an interview to which the department responded with a statement.”







V/O
It states that the process is underway to “implement a total care programme involving the repackaging, transport, treatment and safe disposal of this waste material.”

It also says that “both a civil and criminal case has been instituted by the Department of Water and Sanitation against Guernica” or Thor Chemicals.


Masa
“Prof Naidoo are there any other concerns?”

Rajen
“Next big area of concern to what extent are community members infected and for this we need a public health intervention, we need local government going in and conducting proper assessments of members of the community, understand to what extent people are likely to be affected by the mercury in the community.”

Richard
“So I think its fundamentally a question of money and will, somebody has to come up with the money to clean this up and it is not clear who is going to do that.”

V/O
On a more hopeful note, The Department has said that work has started on packaging the waste for removal. Which was evident when I saw workers in protective gear at one of the dams.

V/O
I asked Chamane what he thought the way forward was.

Musa
“We want to see the workers being compensated for being exposed to this injustice by Thor Chemicals, by gov allowing the chemical giant to come into the country to pollute people, so we want justice.”

Promo 3
Imagine 3 000 one ton bakkies, that is approximately the amount of toxic mercury waste that a chemical company in KZN has been storing (in these warehouses) for over 30 years. Why has nothing been done about it?

In the 1980s after health concerns were raised and the company was therarened with prosecutio, it closed down its operatioons and moved its plant to Cato Ridge KZN, where it opened in 1988 as one of the world’s largest reclamation facilities. At the time, countries around the word were abandoning incineration as a means of processing harzardouse waste but regulations in South Africa were lax. The question is why did a British company such as Thor decide on South Africa to build the largest recycling plant in the world? The obvious answers which spring to mind are: - South Africa's poor environmental protection laws; - cheap and repressed labour; - no established popular environmental non-governmental organisations; - a hope that political outcry over apartheid might leave little time for environmental activities. Within a year, water samples in the nearby Mngweni River showed 1500 times the level considered toxic. By 1992 at least one worker has died from mercury poisoning and there were reports that 28% of the workforce had suffered exposure. Two workers have died. According to the workers that I have interviewed they were not warned of the toxicity of the working envioronment. They also were not proivided with any protective gear. An additional problem was that some of the waste was stolen by people who wanted the drums and possibly by illegal miners. The alarm was raised in the Natal area when three independent investigations, one by the Umgeni Water Board, another by a US newspaper, the St.Louis Post-Dispatch and a third, by the environmental group Greenpeace International, revealed alarmingly high deposits of mercury at the source of the Mngeweni River, just below Thor Chemicals. In an analysis of soil and sediment samples performed by the Queen Mary College in London, a sediment sample was found to be contaminated by 1 764 parts per million of mercury - this is 8 810 times the US standard for classifying the waste as hazardous. River sediment samples at Fredville were also well above the US standard for hazardous wastes. They were taken to hospital as they were "doing and saying strange things, and were shaking a lot". These are typical symptoms of mercury poisoning. The Managing Director at Thor said that workers did get sick but they did not "go mad". "We check the guys* urine every week and if levels exceed 200 micrograms of mercury per litre they are given orange juice to drink and taken away from the plant." Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 11 December 2020 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: Mercury Madness Final Script V/O This is the pastoral Valley of a Thousand Hills, the tranquility of this scene belies a dangerous reality. Livestock from the area drink from this small stream that has been contaminated with the poisonous heavy metal - mercury. V/O And the mercury has come from here, Thor Chemicals a couple of hundred meters up stream. Link REDO BEGINNING OF LINK “These warehouses behind me ARE where hundreds of tons of mercury waste from all over the world have been stored for over 30 years.” V/O Thor Chemicals was a company that made a range of mercury based products and used to be based in Margate, England. Link In the late 70s, Thor left the UK after it had transgressed environmental laws so they packed up , lock stock and barrel and brought what the UK Gov had flagged as health and safety hazards here to South Africa. V/O They opened a plant to recycle mercury waste. And it wasn’t just a barrel or two, it is estimated that over 3000 tons of toxic waste was shipped here from all over the world. To give perspective of the volume imagine 3000 one ton bakkies. http://www.bluebulbprojects.com/measureofthings/results.php?comp=weight&unit=tns&amt=3000&sort=pr&p=1 V/O In the 70’s and 80’s, South Africa’s environmental laws for were quite lax says Musa Chamane. Musa “We did not have any legislation that prevented any waste entering the country or so on, so they took advantage of that policy vaccuum.” V/O Chamane is an environmentalist at GroundWork in Pietermaritzburg. They are one of the organisations that is pressurising the government to take action to prevent more environmental contamination. Link This is the Mngceweni River which flows down from Thor chemicals and makes its way to the Umngeni river, which feeds into the Inanda Dam. Now the last water samples that we made available were done ages ago, so we took some samples of our own. V/O These are two toxic sludge dams on the Thor property and over time mercury from here has leached into the environment, either through the dams overflowing during floods or by accident. V/O Eight samples of soil, sediment and water were sent to Talbot Laboratories in Pietermaritzburg. V/O The fence result was 16.2 (milligrams of mercury per kilogram of soil) showing that there was contamintion across Thor’s fence. The sediment samples in the over flow dam were very high at 330 and 772. Mercury concentrations which exceed 50 mg per kilogram in sediment is classified as chemical waste. V/O Prof Jacques Oosthuizen is an epidemiologist at Edith Cowan University in Perth. He wrote his doctorate on the Thor Chemical’s mercury poisoning and says it is an exceptionally dangerous neurotoxin. https://www.environment.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/situation_analysisof_mercury_sa.pdf (Page 41) Jacques “It affects the nervous system, its blurred vision reduced IQ, problems concentrating, appears person is drunk. Its horrible, its neural and it gets worse over time.” V/O Enock Nkosi who is helping Chamane take water samples, used to work as a chemical process operator at Thor Chemicals and knows first hand how it affects one. Enock ‘Sometimes in the morning I stumble around like I’m drunk but I don’t drink and I don’t smoke. I find myself feeling weak like I am drunk. V/O In 1993 a comission of enquiry was initiated by President Nelson Mandela to probe why the previous government allowed Thor to import the toxic waste. He visited Thor Worker Engelbert Ngcobo in hospital, before he died from mercury poisoning. Judge Dennis Davis, who chaired the Commission found both the apartheid government and Thor complicit. https://www.groundwork.org.za/archives/2019/news20190826-Deadly_Mercury_Injected_into_the_Air.php Enock “I don’t speak as fast as I used to, and now I have a stutter” V/O Many of the tests in the past have focussed on the Thor workers, but can mercury be detected in the community living downstream? The residents do have tap water but some still drink from the river and see as a valuable resource. Chris “The ladies when they have got these cultural things, they often come down here in the morning and go to the river to go and wash themselves.” Sindi “It’s a problem if there is poison in the river because sometimes the kids go and swim in the river and they will be affected.” V/O Sipho Meyiwa is a cow herd for 3 families who have collectively lost 10 cows at the beginning of the year. Sipho ‘When I saw them coming from the river they looked weak and some of them died by the river and we just left them there.” V/O The cow deaths may be anecdotal, but no tests were conducted to see whether the mercury played a part or not. V/O Richard Spoor is a human rights lawyer who has successfully held the mining industry accountable in his billion rand settlement on behalf of the workers who were affected by silicosis. Richard Spoor “Animals dying after drinking contaminated water is a strong indicator that something is wrong in the environment. We have seena lot of this in the Highveld where the cattle have been dying from drinking contaminated water from a waste disposal dams on the coal mines.” V/O To find out if there was any mercury in the hair of residents, cows or goats, samples were taken and sent to the lab. Masa “You have had a look at the samples, what were the results?” Jacques the Carte Blanche samples were detected and their level was 2.6 which is signigicantly higher than the permissable level.” Jacques “It does appear that it is getting through the ecosystem through livestock and I don’t know what levels will be in milk or meat of those animals.” V/O This is Minamata Bay in Japan, where the world’s most horrific mercury poisoning disaster took place. From 1932 – 1968 Chisso Corporation, a fertiliser company, dumped 27 tons of mercury laden waste in the bay. To date over 1700 people have died as the mecury contaminated the whole food chain The mercury caused severe damage to the brain and nervous system, leading to a condition now called Minamata disease. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minamata_disease Tinto “This one guy living next door to me, he got sick and when we came here at work, this guy when he drinks a cup of coffee he will go past his mouth with a cup of coffee he will go this way, and I thought. Whats happening with him, I actually thought he was drunk.” V/O Tinto Summerton worked at Thor Chemicals for about 12 years and he says his health is still severely compromised. Tinto “I only found out when guys were sick that we are dealing with another thing here and there were already 2 guys in hospital and that is when I realised that ay this thing is most dangerous.” V/O In the 80’s Oosthuizen worked at Natal Medical School. Jacques “We became aware of patients that had been admitted into our occupation healthward and they had renal failure, which was attributed to mercury exposure, we then worked out that they all worked at Thor Chemicals.” Tinto “They never told me how dangerous this stuff was, they never even issued me with a mask.” V/O Richard Spoor was employed by NUMSA in the early 90s to represent the Thor Workers against the Department of Labour . Richard “There were a number of deaths and people who were very severly disabled and unequivocally poisoned by mercury, there were also blood tests that demonstrated excessively high levels of mercury in their blood.” Jacques “When the workers got affected the government shut down Thor and told them they can’t operate any more but of course there were ship loads of mercury waste on their way still there and so the stock pile was just growing and growing and drums were rusting and they were leaking and it just became an absolute disaster waiting to happen.” V/O Prof Rajen Naidoo is the Head of UKZN’s Occupational Health Task Team and in the 90’s they monitored the health of the workers. https://disa.ukzn.ac.za/sites/default/files/pdf_files/ChJul92.1024.8196.000.039.Jul1992.17.pdf Masa “Has Thor Chemicals compensated any of the workers?” Rajen “It was fined and the fine that was levied on the company was R 13 500 and subsequently the company was taken to court in the UK courts , they eventually settled out of court and the settlement from which the workers that were affected benefitted.” V/O Thor Chemicals de amalgamated and the local branch was renamed Guernica in 2000 and Metallica, a sister company took over the Cato Ridge Facility. In the UK settlement, Thor paid 240 000 pounds for the 20 workers who claimed they were victims of mercury poisoning. https://allafrica.com/stories/201909030225.html https://www.newframe.com/thor-chemicals-toxic-waste-goes-up-in-flames/ Tinto “We only got money that just helped us to be able to go to the doctors and I wouldn’t even call it a compensation but it helped us, we are still alive.” V/O We requested an interview with Thor Chemicals and sent them a list of questions. They answered by saying, “The legacy mercury stockpile is under the authority of the Department of Environment, Forestry and Fisheries.” And we should direct our queries to them. V/O They did however call the police when they saw the film crew outside their fence. Up Sound “I have been watching you. If we have a break in I am going to hold you responsible.” V/O Both Governments have failed to hold Thor accountable. There are no local facilities capable of recycling this waste, there have been proposals of entombing the waste in concrete forever or shipping it back to the senders or to a company in Switzerland for recycling at a cost of about R330 million. https://allafrica.com/stories/201909030225.html https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/sunday-times-1107/20190901/281784220766799 Richard “The government needs to take action against the South African subsideries and compel them to clean up and they simply havent done that. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Creecy Link Minister of Environmental Affairs, Forestry and Fisheries, Barbara Creecy went on a fact finding mission in August last year and she said, and I quote, “This is a scandal and a gross irresponsibility on the part of Thor Chemicals.” https://www.enca.com/news/thor-chemicals-must-clean-mess-creecy V/O Less than 2 weeks after the Minister’s visit, a fire broke out in a warehouse storing the mercury waste. It is estimated that as much as 30 tons of mercury was injected into the environment as a result of the fire. https://www.ban.org/news/2019/8/26/deadly-mercury-injected-into-the-air-a-very-convenient-fire-governments-failure-means-thor-chemicals-will-never-be-held-accountable Link “A year later it seems nothing has happened. We asked the Minister for an interview to which the department responded with a statement.” V/O It states that the process is underway to “implement a total care programme involving the repackaging, transport, treatment and safe disposal of this waste material.” It also says that “both a civil and criminal case has been instituted by the Department of Water and Sanitation against Guernica” or Thor Chemicals. Masa “Prof Naidoo are there any other concerns?” Rajen “Next big area of concern to what extent are community members infected and for this we need a public health intervention, we need local government going in and conducting proper assessments of members of the community, understand to what extent people are likely to be affected by the mercury in the community.” Richard “So I think its fundamentally a question of money and will, somebody has to come up with the money to clean this up and it is not clear who is going to do that.” V/O On a more hopeful note, The Department has said that work has started on packaging the waste for removal. Which was evident when I saw workers in protective gear at one of the dams. V/O I asked Chamane what he thought the way forward was. Musa “We want to see the workers being compensated for being exposed to this injustice by Thor Chemicals, by gov allowing the chemical giant to come into the country to pollute people, so we want justice.” Promo 1 People have died from mercury poisoning and still a chemical company in KZN stores about 3000 tons of toxic mercury waste in these warehouses. A fire last year brought the whole environmental travesty to light. Promo 2 South Africa was used as a dumping ground in the 80’s and we now have thousands of tons of mercury waste in a warehouse in Cato Ridge. The chemicals have leached into the environment and into the food chain. Promo 3 Imagine 3 000 one ton bakkies, that is approximately the amount of toxic mercury waste that a chemical company in KZN has been storing (in these warehouses) for over 30 years. Why has nothing been done about it? Promo 1 People have died from mercury poisoning and still a chemical company in KZN stores about 3000 tons of toxic mercury waste here. A fire last year brought the whole environmental travesty to light. Promo 2 South Africa was used as a dumping ground in the 80’s and we now have thousands of tons of mercury waste in a warehouse in KZN. The chemicals have leached into the environment and into the food chain. Promo 3 Imagine 3 000 one ton bakkies, that’s about the amount of toxic mercury waste that a chemical company in KZN has been stored here for decades. Why has nothing been done about it?

metadata.Further information: Mercury has been poisoning workers and the environment for over 30 years. Even though there has been a comission of enquiry and interventions by the Government the mercury stock pile still exists. In September last year it was reported that ; Thor Chemicals to pay R300m to remove its deadly mercury waste from KZN The department of environmental affairs says it wants more than 3,000 tons of mercury waste stockpiles at the old Thor Chemicals factory in KwaZulu-Natal to be removed by the end of next year. The department says Thor Chemicals — a British multinational that owned and ran the Cato Ridge plant where drums of toxic sludge are stored — has agreed in principle to pay more than R300m required to export the waste to Switzerland, where it will be disposed of. Mercury is a powerful neurotoxin, which can lead to blurred vision, tremors, brain damage, coma and death. In the late 1980s and 1990s, scores of Thor Chemicals workers who were exposed to the hazardous chemical waste were diagnosed with mercury poisoning and died painful deaths. Others were partially poisoned and are still feeling the effect of this poisoning, decades later. Thor Chemicals moved its mercury incinerator plant from Margate, Kent, in the UK in the mid-70s after an outcry about the hazardous nature of the operation. The company then began exporting these chemicals to its Cato Ridge facility. The plant was forced to shut its doors here in the early 1990s after news that workers poisoned by mercury were dying and others were comatose. The plant has been in a state of dilapidation since then. Two incidents have shone the spotlight on the plant in recent months. Criminals stole some containers of the toxic substance in the hope of using it in zama-zama mining pursuits and other criminal activities. A few weeks ago, a fire broke out at the facility, and environmental organisations estimate that more than 30 tons of mercury waste was injected into the environment as a result of the fire. In August 2019, the minister of environmental affairs, forestry and fisheries, Barbara Creecy, promised to take immediate action to ensure that the chemicals were moved from the site and destroyed. Albi Modise, spokesperson for the department, said talks between government officials and Thor Chemicals are at an advanced stage. “Our laws stipulate that the perpetrator must pay for the cleanup. Minister has made it clear that this mercury-containing waste must be disposed of appropriately and expeditiously. The option proposed by Thor Chemicals entails the removal of the waste to a company that is based in Switzerland. This company has a sound track record of dealing with mercury and mercury-containing waste and has the necessary capacity and authorisations to do so. The department’s primary concern is the safe and expeditious disposal of the waste to avoid any environmental harm,” Modise said. Neville Naicker, a director of Thor Chemicals SA subsidery, Guernica has in the past declined to speak to journalists. Bobby Peek, director of environmental lobby group groundWork, said pressure from local environmental organisations on the one hand and local communities on the other had forced the government to finally take action after more than two decades of neglect. “We have always maintained that the waste stockpiles can only be treated outside SA because we have never had the facilities to deal with mercury toxic waste locally. This mercurial waste should never have come to SA in the first place. The toxic waste sludge is made up of a mixture of mercury sludge, arsenic and other organic compounds, making it difficult to treat,” Peek said. He added that the government must also consider the plight of scores of former Thor Chemicals workers. “There are many [former] workers and families who were affected by the Thor Chemicals operation and we believe they have never received a just and fair long-term settlement commensurate with the loss they suffered,” he said.
